Create outcome model arguments

Source: R/OutcomeModels.R
createOutcomeModelArgs.Rd

Specifies all parameters for [fitOutcomeModel()], which fits a regression model for the outcome on the matched (or stratified) study population.

Usage

createOutcomeModelArgs(
  modelType = "cox",
  stratified = TRUE,
  useCovariates = FALSE,
  prior = NULL,
  control = NULL
)

Arguments

modelType

(`character(1)`) One of `"cox"` (default), `"logistic"`, or `"poisson"`.

stratified

(`logical(1)`) Whether to stratify by `stratumId` (matched set). `TRUE` (default) uses conditional Cox / logistic / Poisson; `FALSE` fits an unconditional model. Stratification requires that [matchOnTcps()] has been run.

useCovariates

(`logical(1)`) If `TRUE`, include all covariates from `pnuData` as additional adjusters in the outcome model (doubly-robust approach). Default: `FALSE`.

prior

(`cyclopsPrior`) Cyclops prior for the covariate coefficients when `useCovariates = TRUE`. The treatment coefficient is always unpenalised. Ignored when `useCovariates = FALSE`. `NULL` uses a Laplace prior with cross-validation.

control

(`cyclopsControl`) Cyclops control specification. `NULL` uses the Cyclops default.

Value

An `OutcomeModelArgs` R6 object.

References

Suissa S, Moodie EE, Dell'Aniello S. Prevalent new-user cohort designs for comparative drug effect studies by time-conditional propensity scores. *Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf* 2017;26(4):459-468. doi:10.1002/pds.4117

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Default: stratified Cox, treatment effect only
outcomeModelArgs <- createOutcomeModelArgs()

# Doubly-robust: also adjust for covariates in the outcome model
outcomeModelArgs <- createOutcomeModelArgs(useCovariates = TRUE)
} # }
